Definition: from G4687; something sown, i.e. seed (including the male "sperm"); by implication, offspring; specially, a remnant (figuratively, as if kept over for planting):--issue, seed.
BiblicalUsage: Seed is offspring, and the promise runs on it. To Abraham and his seed were the promises made, not to seeds as of many, but as of one, and to thy seed, which is Christ; in Isaac shall thy seed be called; in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed; and the seed of God remaineth in the one born of God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the seed narrows to one man and then widens to all nations, and I hold that everyone born of God carries that seed within. The promise to Abraham stands because the Seed is Christ, and all who are His share in it.
